thread:
maya: hitting a customer bug — SSE stream returns everything but the final JSON object after an idle reauth. Customer sees a well-formed JSON stream up until the last chunk which never arrives. finish_reason is absent.

sam: is this consistently reproducible for them or intermittent? any proxies in front?

maya: reproducible 3/3 on their staging. path: prod gateway -> our auth-proxy -> inference. They have an idle token refresh that re-POSTs auth and we rotate tokens during long-lived streams.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro or curl output? will try to hit it locally.
\nmaya: here's a trimmed client capture (sanitized):
```
> GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-alpha HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer REUSED_TOKEN
> Accept: text/event-stream

< 200 OK
< event: data
< data: {"chunk":"hello "}
< data: {"chunk":"world"}
< data: {"chunk":"!"}
< 
# then after ~90s idle auth refresh happens on their side
# client reconnects with resume header: `x-resume-from: 3`
< 200 OK
< event: data
< data: {"chunk":"more"}
# stream ends abruptly, no final `data: {"finish_reason":...}` and no trailing "}]"
```

anita: do we see any 4xx/5xx from our auth-proxy logs at the same window? can we get the proxy request/response pairs?

maya: proxy logs show 200s for the auth refresh, nothing obviously wrong. but our gateway trace shows connection closed by upstream during final flush. attaching snippet: `upstream WRITE: 0 bytes, ECONNRESET`

sam: interesting. two hypotheses: 1) client reconnect drops the final frame because our resume path doesn't re-emit terminal sentinel, 2) some TCP proxy (nginx/ELB) closes connection right after token swap and drops last bytes.

maya: customer repro steps (short):
- start stream with token A
- let stream be idle for ~60-120s
- rotate token on client, reconnect with resume header
- observe missing terminal object and no finish_reason

sam: can you run this curl repro? I've used this locally to simulate: 
```bash
# open event stream (simulate client's reconnect flow)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer A" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test" | sed -n '1,20p'
# then after idle, do a second request with resume header
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer B" -H "x-resume-from: 3" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test" | sed -n '1,20p'
```

maya: ran that, I see the second connection returns but the final `finish_reason` chunk is gone ~40% of attempts.

anita: tagging eng-runtime and eng-infra. @sam can you capture a tcpdump around the gateway when you run the curl? need to see if the final bytes are sent from runtime before the reset.

sam: will do. quick workaround for customer: increase stream keepalive or send periodic noop tokens so the rotate doesn't coincide with final flush. also recommend disabling immediate connection close on token swap at their proxy.

maya: customer asked if this is a billing/usage issue — they worry about charges for incomplete responses. billing: partial token usage already billed; but we should avoid leaving a customer with unusable output.

anita: agreed. let's make this P1 until we have a mitigations doc. I'll open INC and assign oncall.

replay-bot: incident INC-2247 created: sse-terminal-drop-on-auth-rotate. Assigned to eng-runtime oncall. https://pager.redwood.example/INC-2247

sam: preliminary findings: when resume header is present we rehydrate kv-cache and stream from runtime; if upstream socket gets an RST during the terminal flush, the final sentinel byte sequence can be lost because it's sent in the same TCP segment as the FIN. Need to ensure kernel socket uses SO_LINGER=0? or better: flush+drain before closing.

maya: next actions for support: 1) send customer the curl repro and suggested keepalive workaround, 2) collect tcpdump and full proxy logs, 3) await eng-runtime fix. I'll update the ticket with logs and repro. :thumbsup:

anita: also add a short console warning in the docs about resume + auth rotations and recommend the `x-resume-from` be used only with sticky tokens where possible.

sam: will prototype a runtime change to explicitly send terminal sentinel in a separate TCP packet (force flush) and add retries on resume path. assigning follow-up PR to runtime team.

maya: thanks team — customer notified of workaround. will paste their confirmation in the ticket when they verify.

sam: keeping this thread open for updates.
